candidates.new:
STA sky_j8
    LDX #0
.row
    LDA sky_j8                      \ sky_col_row's tests, inline (its caller here only): sk = this column from the entry's first
    SEC
    SBC sky_rc,X
    BCC next                        \ before it
    STA sky_stop
    CMP sky_ry,X
    BCC chk1_in                     \ sk < the last
    BNE next                        \ after it
.chk1_in
    LDA sky_rt,X                    \ the cells' bytes lie at rl + (rt | sk) - (rn - 1) .. rl + (rt | sk): s_ptr = the lowest
    ORA sky_stop                    \ (rn <= rt + 1, so 0 or more)
    SEC
    SBC sky_rn,X
    INC A                           \ 65C02 opcode
    CLC
    ADC sky_rl,X
    STA s_ptr
    LDA sky_rh,X
    ADC #0
    STA s_ptr + 1
    LDY sky_rn,X
    DEY                             \ rn - 1 down to 0 (rn is 1 to 8)
    LDA (s_ptr),Y
    DEY
    BMI chk1_done
.byte
    ORA (s_ptr),Y                   \ all the bytes ORed: nothing exits early, as nothing is ever found
    DEY
    BPL byte
.chk1_done
    TAY
    BNE dirty
.next
    INX
    CPX sky_nq
    BNE row
    CLC
    RTS
.dirty
    SEC
    RTS
candidates.summary: sky_col_check does its own row setup (a copy of sky_col_row's tests, no JSR/RTS) and points s_ptr at the row's lowest byte (rl + (rt|sk) - rn + 1, 16-bit), so the byte loop counts Y from rn-1 to 0 with DEY/BPL (no CPY sky_stop) and ORs the bytes together, testing once per row (TAY/BNE dirty). Byte loop 15 -> 10 cycles a byte, row setup 71 -> 60. sky_col_row and its other callers untouched. Alternative to the second candidate (overlaps it).
candidates.equivalence: Same answer: C set iff some byte of some entry's column is non-zero. The entry tests are sky_col_row's (BCC no when j8 < rc; no when ry < sk: here CMP ry vs sk, BCC = sk < ry, BNE = sk > ry, equal passes). The bytes read are the same set of addresses: the original reads rl + Ystart - k for k = 0..rn-1 with Ystart = rt|sk (Y counting down from it to stop+1, stop = Ystart - rn); the new s_ptr = rl + (Ystart - rn + 1) (mod 256 in A, which is the true value since the builder has rn <= rt + 1: bottom row rn = L + 1, rt = L; whole rows rn = 8, rt = 7; the top row rn = t <= 8, rt = 7; split copies keep both) with the carry into the high byte, and Y = rn-1 .. 0 reads s_ptr + Y = the same addresses (16-bit add by the hardware, same &7FFF/&8000 behaviour as before since the addresses are identical). Dirty: any byte non-zero ORs into A, TAY sets Z, BNE dirty; the original stopped at the first non-zero, this finishes the row first, with no other side effect (reads only). Exits: CLC/RTS after the last entry, SEC/RTS when dirty, as before. Not live after: X, Y, A, Z/N/V (the only caller path is JMP sky_col_check from lead_col, whose callers do BCS fall and reload A, X), s_ptr, sky_stop, sky_j8 (all written before read at every use). Python model of old vs new over 200,000 random tables and memory contents agreed on every one. rn = 1: LDA, DEY gives $FF, BMI taken, TAY tests the one byte.
candidates.relies_on: No page-crossing moves: sky_col_check is the last code of hazel_b (nothing after it in the section), the new code is 70 bytes against 27 so hazel_b_end goes &DF65 -> &DF90 (test-assembled) (below the &E000 ASSERT; the gameplay builds' hazel_b_end is &DF65 too), the byte loop is at &DF7F-&DF85 and every branch is inside page &DF (BNE row within 127 bytes). The file after hazel_b (hazel_c's load image, the packed tunes) slides 37 bytes in the start-up block, which has 1,500 bytes free (mgame_end &4E36). The sky_r* tables are at &BC90-&BCB5, X is at most 5, no indexed read crosses a page (as before). The (s_ptr),Y reads cross a page only when the address span does: never more often than before (the old base was rl, so any rl + Y >= 256 paid). Uses 65C02 INC A (the file already does). Requires rn between 1 and rt + 1 for every entry, which the builder guarantees (checked above); the original would loop 256 times with rn = 0 and read wrong bytes if rn > rt + 1.

candidates.old:
JSR sky_col_row
    BCS next
.byte
    LDA (s_ptr),Y
    BNE dirty
    DEY
    CPY sky_stop
    BNE byte
candidates.new:
JSR sky_col_row
    BCS next
    LDA (s_ptr),Y                   \ the bytes ORed, so the loop has no exit but its end
    DEY
    CPY sky_stop
    BEQ chk2_done
.byte
    ORA (s_ptr),Y
    DEY
    CPY sky_stop
    BNE byte
.chk2_done
    TAY
    BNE dirty
candidates.summary: Keeps the JSR sky_col_row contract; the byte loop ORs the bytes (LDA first, then ORA (s_ptr),Y / DEY / CPY sky_stop / BNE) and tests once per row (TAY / BNE dirty): 15 -> 13 cycles a byte, 4 more a row. Smaller change than the first candidate (+8 bytes); alternative to it (overlaps it).
candidates.equivalence: Same reads at the same addresses: first LDA at Y, then DEY / CPY stop / loop until Y == stop, as the do-while before (rn >= 1 so the first byte is always read; if the first DEY reaches stop the BEQ leaves with that one byte read). ORA accumulates; TAY sets Z from the OR of all the bytes of the row: BNE dirty exits with C set (the SEC/RTS at .dirty) exactly when the original would have, only after finishing the row (reads only, no side effects). X unchanged through the loop; Y is free after. Rows skipped by BCS next take the same path. A, Y, Z not live after the row (next row's JSR sky_col_row loads A, sets Y).
candidates.relies_on: sky_col_check is the last code in hazel_b: nothing after it moves its alignment (hazel_b_end &DF65 -> &DF6D, below &E000; the start-up block after it slides 8 bytes). The byte loop (LDA at &DF53 before) stays in page &DF, so BNE byte, BEQ and BNE dirty do not cross a page (loop about &DF5B-&DF63). The (s_ptr),Y reads are the same addresses as before, so the same page crossings.
